 Most recent Most popular 'It's always tough when you play Stoke' published at 12:27 GMT 12:27 GMT 
 Portsmouth v Stoke (12:30 GMT) 
 Guy Whittingham 
Former Portsmouth striker and manager on BBC Radio Solent 
 It's a lot stronger today for Portsmouth and we have players to come back which bodes well for the future.
 Stoke are a strong side. They've spent in the summer and have £10m sitting on the bench in George Hirst who they nabbed off us. It's going to be a tough game, it's always tough when you play Stoke.
 Portsmouth should be confident today with how they played against Swansea. It's about winning the one-on-one battles on the pitch.

 Tale of the tape published at 12:25 GMT 12:25 GMT 
 Wrexham v Wolves (12:30 GMT) 
 Ian Mitchelmore 
BBC Sport Wales at the Racecourse Ground, Wrexham 
 Wrexham are seeking a third consecutive home win having beaten bottom side Preston North End and leaders Middlesbrough in their past two games here at the Racecourse Ground.
 But Phil Parkinson's men have another tough task ahead of them today as they face a Wolves side that are unbeaten in five games.
 Cesar Peixoto's men come into today's fixture having won three successive league games.
 They have not won four league matches in a row since winning six on the spin in the Premier League between March and April in 2025.

 One change for Wrexham, five for Wolves published at 12:24 GMT 12:24 GMT 
 Wrexham v Wolves (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Opta Wrexham make one change as Ollie Rathbone comes in for Wednesday's goalscorer George Thomason.
 Five changes for Wolves with defender Nasser Djiga making his first appearance since picking up a muscle injury last month.
 Rodrigo Gomes also makes a first start since his return from an ankle issue that led him to miss four games in October.
 Jackson Tchatchoua and Mateus Mane also join the XI.
 Kieran Trippier, Yerson Mosquera, Hugo Bueno, Jean-Ricner Bellegarde and Rafiki Said rotate to the bench.
 Image source, Opta

 Wrexham's dragons flip the script published at 12:22 GMT 12:22 GMT 
 Wrexham v Wolves (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Getty Images Heroes may like to slay a dragon in folklore but over in the town of Wrexham, it's the dragon who does the conquering of a bigger, mightier foe.
 The Red Dragons have claimed four Championship wins so far this season and while that is nowhere near the number they would like, two of those those victories came against the very best the league has to offer.
 They claimed a 2-0 win over league leaders Middlesbrough in midweek and also triumphed 2-1 against Southampton, the side who would be top of the table if it weren't for their-four point deduction for Spygate. Both came at the Stok Cae Ras.
 Now they host second-placed Wolves, a hungry predator attempting to take their place at the apex.
 Will the Racecourse be feasting on the bones of another giant come full-time? And is that fog over the Stok Cae Ras - or a dragon's smoky breath?
 Image source, Shutterstock

 Pompey change two; Potters swap three published at 12:18 GMT 12:18 GMT 
 Portsmouth v Stoke (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Opta John Mousinho has made two changes to the Pompey XI which
left it late to beat Swansea 3-1at Fratton Park on Tuesday.
 Marlon Pack and Abu Kamara come in with Marko Milovanovic
and Iyad Mohamed missing out after coming off against the Swans.
 Mark Robins has changed three of the Potters side which won
2-1 at Blackburn the same night.
 Bosun Lawal, Junior Tchamadeu and Ethan Galbraith return

 In-form Blues and Potters in lunchtime showdown published at 12:16 GMT 12:16 GMT 
 Portsmouth v Stoke (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Shutterstock Red-hot Stoke will aim to go top of the Championship when they take on in-form Portsmouth at Fratton Park.
 Pompey themselves are seeking a seventh game unbeaten after their 3-1 win over Swansea on Tuesday night and could jump as high as sixth if results go their way.
 The Potters are fourth after Tuesday's 2-1 win at Blackburn made it 26 points earned from their past 11 games and a victory, coupled with Wolves failing to win at Wrexham in another early-kick off, would see Mark Robins' side take over at the summit, for a couple of hours at least.
 Not bad for a side who lost all three of their opening league games this season - after losing the final four in a row last term too, a run of seven straight defeats overall.
 This one should be fascinating.

 Dickie back for Robins, Norwich make one change published at 12:14 GMT 12:14 GMT 
 Bristol City v Norwich (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Opta Defender Rob Dickie returns to the Bristol City line-up for the first time since he injured his knee in mid-September.
 Dickie replaces Luke McNally in the Robins' back line, with one other change as Adam Randell comes in for Sam Bell, who drops to the bench. Striker Elijah Adebayo is also among the substitutes after returning from injury.
 Norwich boss Philippe Clement makes just a single change to the side that triumphed 4-0 at Derby in midweek, with Ben Chrisene back in the left-back slot ahead of Darlin Yongwa.
 Image source, Opta

 Can Robins rediscover home comforts against in-form Norwich? published at 12:12 GMT 12:12 GMT 
 Bristol City v Norwich (12:30 GMT) 
 Image source, Shutterstock Home, sweet home? Ashton Gate hasn’t
really sparked that kind of sentiment for most of the Bristol City faithful so
far this season.
 City have been beaten in each of their past three outings on home soil and five times in seven overall – most recently
when they squandered a 1-0 lead to Wolves in the last 10 minutes on Tuesday
night.
 Perhaps the last thing Michael Skubala’s
side need in those circumstances is a visit from resurgent Norwich, who have
won three games on the spin following a poor start to the campaign.
 Just three weeks ago, the Canaries were
perched precariously just above the bottom three after a run of five straight
defeats, but they are now in the top half after that trio of wins and 10 goals
to boot.
 “We know we can score goals,” head
coach Philippe Clement told BBC Radio Norfolk after their midweek thumping of
Derby. “But now we're starting to become more and more of a team.”

 Tussle for top spot going into break published at 12:10 GMT 12:10 GMT 
 Championship 
 Image source, Opta/Shutterstock What more could you ask for? Six teams go into the final game before the second international break of the season with a chance to sit top of the pile in the second tier over the two-week interruption.
 Wolves have the first bite of the cherry in their early kick-off at Wrexham but should they fail to win then Stoke can take over at the top if they can earn three points at Portsmouth, also at 12:30 GMT.
 Middlesbrough have the chance to answer back when they head to Watford later on, while Birmingham, or even their visitors Swansea, could take over in first with a win and other results going their way.
 Even West Bromwich Albion, in sixth, could finish the day top although that would take an unlikely set of results and a goal difference swing.
 Southampton and West Ham will aim to closer the gap this afternoon when they face Millwall, Preston and Blackburn respectively while at the foot of the table Charlton, Lincoln and Cardiff will seek breathing space as they take on Sheffield United, QPR and Burnley respectively.
 Got a feeling this could be an extraordinary day in the Championship.

 Preview: Contenders, pretenders and strugglers published at 12:08 GMT 12:08 GMT 
 Championship 
 Image source, Shutterstock Image caption, Based on the past six matches, Chris Davies' Birmingham City are first and Sheffield United fifth in the Championship form table
 With League One and League Two clubs involved in the FA Cup this weekend, the Championship has a free run of the EFL.
 So far, England's second tier has served up its usual helping of drama and chaos in equal measure while sacking season seems to be in full swing.
 We have picked out five things you may want to keep an eye out for this afternoon.
 Click here to discover what they are.

 About last night... published at 12:06 GMT 12:06 GMT 
 FT: Derby 3-1 Bolton 
 Image source, Shutterstock John Eustace's hopes of keeping his job at Derby got a huge boost last night as the Rams produced a scintillating second-half fightback to beat Bolton and end a 10-game winless run. 
 There was disquiet before Ruben Rodrigues put the visitors ahead with his cool finish late in the first half, and boos from the Rams faithful eventually greeted the half-time whistle at Pride Park.
 But two goals in the first four minutes of the second half from Ryan Nyambe and Jack Robinson transformed the atmosphere and quite possibly Eustace's fate. 
 Rams goalkeeper Jacob Widell Zetterstrom went on to make a number of crucial saves to keep the hosts ahead before Rhian Brewster made sure of just their second Championship win of the season in stoppage time with a fierce finish.
 Click here for the match report.

 Good afternoon! published at 12:00 GMT 12:00 GMT 
 Championship 
 Image source, Getty Images If you thought the fireworks had been and gone, maybe think again.
 By bedtime tonight we'll be basically a third of the way through the Championship season and the battle for the title, and promotion places, might just be the tightest there has been at this stage of a second-tier campaign.
 We have 11 games to bring you this afternoon, three of them kick-off in just under half an hour, and all the main protagonists will have their turn on the stage.
 In the final game of one of these gruelling 'nine-point weeks', and with a fortnight's international break to come, it's the perfect day to turn up.
 We have plenty to get through so best we bring you up to speed quickly...
